analyzed_vuln.description: The bug is an out-of-bounds read during AAT kerx table sanitization when parsing a Lookup table with unsupported format 10. In Lookup<T>::sanitize(), the code reads u.format (2 bytes) and then switches only on formats {0,2,4,6,8}; any other format falls through to default and returns true (accepted) without validating the actual structure size for that format. Later, KerxSubTableFormat6 sanitization follows an OffsetTo<Lookup<...>> and LookupFormat10 data is effectively treated as sanitized, leading to reads past the blob end (crash observed in BEInt<unsigned short>::operator unsigned short() from LookupFormat10::sanitize path). Root cause is missing/incorrect format validation and bounds checks for non-enumerated lookup formats in Lookup::sanitize, not the low-level BEInt read site.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Triggered from hb-shape-fuzzer with a crafted font containing a kerx table, specifically a kerx subtable format 6 whose lookup offset points to a lookup blob declaring format 10 near end-of-buffer/truncated data. Because Lookup::sanitize accepts unknown format values, malformed/truncated format-10 lookup content is not rejected early; subsequent kerx/lookup sanitization logic dereferences fields beyond the 69-byte input allocation, causing a 1-byte heap OOB read.
